title: Lutein inhibits ferroptosis and reduces neuronal cell death induced by Parkinson's disease through the NRF2-HMOX2 signaling axis.
authors: Duan, Jiabin; Duan, Wenbin; Pu, Xiaomin; Ma, Changdi; Huang, Huai; Xu, Zhenghu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究叶黄素通过NRF2-HMOX2信号轴抑制帕金森病神经元铁死亡，属于疾病机制与药物保护研究，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to investigate the role of lutein in the inhibition of ferroptosis in neurons induced by Parkinson's disease (PD) and the underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: PD animal and cellular models were established by the intraperitoneal injection of 1-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine (MPTP) in mice and treatment with 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP(+)) in SH-SY5Y cells. Behavioral tests, immunohistochemistry, and hematoxylin-eosin (HE) staining were employed to evaluate motor function and neuronal damage. Oxidative stress and ferroptosis-related markers were assessed using commercial assay kits and flow cytometry. RESULTS: Lutein treatment significantly alleviated MPTP-induced motor deficits in PD model mice and increased the number of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neurons. Furthermore, lutein attenuated MPTP/MPP(+)-induced neuronal ferroptosis, as indicated by decreased Fe(2+) and ACSL4 levels and elevated FTH1 and SLC7A11 expression-all of which were reversed by the ferroptosis activator erastin. Molecular docking and Western blot analyses demonstrated that lutein upregulated SOD1/2 and GPX1/2/3 expression. Notably, lutein treatment increased SOD and GSH levels while reducing MDA and ROS levels, indicating its neuroprotective role via antioxidant activation. Mechanistically, exposure to MPTP/MPP(+) markedly suppressed NRF2 and HMOX2 expression, whereas lutein restored these levels; this protective effect was diminished by the NRF2 inhibitor ML385, which counteracted the suppression of oxidative stress and ferroptosis by lutein. CONCLUSION: Lutein reduces dopaminergic neuronal death by promoting the expression of SOD1/2 and GPX1/2/3 and inhibiting PD ferroptosis through the activation of the NRF2-HMOX2 signaling pathway.
abstract_zh: 目的：本研究旨在探讨叶黄素在抑制帕金森病（PD）诱导的神经元铁死亡中的作用及其潜在分子机制。方法：通过小鼠腹腔注射1-甲基-4-苯基-1,2,3,6-四氢吡啶（MPTP）和SH-SY5Y细胞处理1-甲基-4-苯基吡啶（MPP(+)）建立PD动物和细胞模型。采用行为学测试、免疫组织化学和苏木精-伊红（HE）染色评估运动功能和神经元损伤。使用商业检测试剂盒和流式细胞术评估氧化应激和铁死亡相关标志物。结果：叶黄素处理显著缓解了PD模型小鼠中MPTP诱导的运动缺陷，并增加了酪氨酸羟化酶（TH）阳性神经元的数量。此外，叶黄素减弱了MPTP/MPP(+)诱导的神经元铁死亡，表现为Fe(2+)和ACSL4水平降低，FTH1和SLC7A11表达升高——所有这些均被铁死亡激活剂erastin逆转。分子对接和Western blot分析表明，叶黄素上调了SOD1/2和GPX1/2/3的表达。值得注意的是，叶黄素处理增加了SOD和GSH水平，同时降低了MDA和ROS水平，表明其通过抗氧化激活发挥神经保护作用。机制上，暴露于MPTP/MPP(+)显著抑制了NRF2和HMOX2的表达，而叶黄素恢复了这些水平；这种保护效应被NRF2抑制剂ML385削弱，该抑制剂抵消了叶黄素对氧化应激和铁死亡的抑制作用。结论：叶黄素通过促进SOD1/2和GPX1/2/3的表达，并通过激活NRF2-HMOX2信号通路抑制PD铁死亡，从而减少多巴胺能神经元死亡。
